resources.string: JustType is an accessible 8-key keyboard for people who find a normal touchscreen keyboard hard to use. It predicts the words you want, and works with direct touch, swiping, switches, a joystick, or head movement.\n\nThis short guide turns JustType on and helps you choose the input method that fits. A caregiver can help with setup.

First, turn JustType on in your device's keyboard settings:

1. Tap "Open keyboard settings" and switch on JustType Keyboard, then come back here.
2. Tap "Switch keyboard" and choose JustType.

The line below shows whether JustType is enabled yet.

You\'re ready to type! Open any text box and JustType will appear.\n\nNot sure which input method to use? Tap below for help choosing. You can reopen this guide or open Input Methods anytime from JustType Settings.

Drives your device with the same 8-key grid. A small floating keyboard appears on top of any app; arrow keys move focus, and other keys perform actions like Tap and Back.

When on, DRAG holds the target down and moves it in real time as you press the arrows, dropping it where it lands. When off, you aim a cursor first and the move happens all at once when you press DROP.

Chooses which spelling is offered first where British and American English differ — colour/color, centre/center, realise/realize — and which regional words rank higher, such as lorry or apartment.\n\nBOTH spellings are always available whichever you pick; the other one simply appears further down the list. GENERAL offers them in plain frequency order.

Chooses how much coarse language is left out of the word predictions.

OFFENSIVE WORDS (the default) leaves out common swearing and crude terms.

POTENTIALLY OFFENSIVE WORDS also leaves out milder words that some people find objectionable, such as anatomical and sexual terms.

NONE offers every word in the dictionary, including all of the above.

Racial, ethnic, religious and anti-LGBTQ slurs are never predicted at any setting. Whatever you choose here, you can always add any word you like to your own vocabulary.

Shows likely next words in the selection list based on the previous word, before and while you type. Turning this off restores the frequency-only list.
Signals you when the top list item is probably your word, so you can stop typing and select it. Requires Context Predictions.
How the signal is delivered: a short rising beep, a green flash on the Select key, or both.
How sure JustType must be before signaling. Higher values signal less often and are almost always right; lower values signal more often and can save more keystrokes.

How the word list balances predictions against a fixed, learnable order. Predictive: the most likely words lead, using the words you typed before — fewest keystrokes (recommended). Steady first word: the first slot always shows the same word for the same keys; predictions follow (roughly 7–15% more keystrokes). Steady start: the first two slots are fixed (roughly 16–33% more). Classic: no predictions at all — the list depends only on the keys you typed, like classic JustType (roughly 40–69% more). Prediction settings below are inactive in Classic.

If the signal is going to interrupt you, it should be right at least this often. JustType measures its own accuracy on your typing and tunes the signal to meet your target. Higher settings make the signal more trustworthy but rarer.
The Confidence Signal could have saved you %1$d keystrokes. You can turn it on in Settings, under Word Selection.

Where the tone-mark key is pressed when typing a syllable. End of syllable is the standard Telex/VNI convention. After tone vowel enters the tone immediately after its vowel — candidates before the tone show unmarked vowels, and the tone keys display the possible vowel forms. Changing this rebuilds the dictionary index.

Chooses which accented letters Letter Spell Mode offers when you pick a base letter. \"From current typing language\" shows only the accents used by the language you are typing in; \"From all downloaded typing languages\" includes every language on your device; \"All\" shows every accent; \"None\" shows none. Each language\'s accents are learned automatically from its words.
UI Feedback Language Voice Type Preference

Your preferred voice type for UI feedback — the voice that speaks prompts, key names, and announcements to you. Some users choose the opposite of their personal voice type so system feedback is easy to tell apart from their own spoken words. Used to suggest and default the UI Feedback Voice.

Your preferred voice type. JustType uses it to suggest a voice when you choose one for a language. Availability depends on the speech engines installed on your device, and the match is a best guess — use Test to confirm. Child voices in particular are uncommon.

When enabled, picking a letter in Letter Spell Mode opens a variant page so you can pick an accented form (á, ä, etc.). When disabled, only the base letter is entered and Spell Mode stays at a fixed two keystrokes per character.
When enabled, less common variants (ā, ů, ǔ, etc.) are added to the variant page alongside common ones. Requires \"Show diacritics in Spell Mode\" to be on.

Vietnamese-specific variants (ư, ầ, ằ, etc.) are independent from common / uncommon. Include adds them to the variant page sorted to the front; Only shows just Vietnamese-tagged variants (and hides everything else).
When enabled, i uppercases to İ (dotted capital) and ı uppercases to I (plain), regardless of system locale. Useful when typing Turkish or Azerbaijani in a non-Turkish system locale.
Use touchscreen settings for backup and restore operations

How the selection list is ordered. Blocks (default): fully-typed words always come first, then completions. FTS Pin: the top fully-typed word keeps slot 1, everything else is ordered purely by sort metric. Interleave: the whole list is ordered by sort metric. Fully-typed words are always listed under every policy.

When on (default), words with all letters typed and only the tone keystroke remaining are guaranteed a place above letter-incomplete completions. When off they compete by sort metric like any other completion. Only affects tone-keystroke languages.

Adaptive FTS promotion ladder. Observe (default): record Select-press patterns only, no behavior change. Force Page 1 / Force Head: at a Select press with no confidence signal, fully-typed words sitting below the head are promoted onto page 1 or into the head. Adaptive: reserved — observes only until the automatic ramp ships.

When on (default), after JustType crashes, opening Settings offers to email a crash report. The report includes only the error and your device model — never anything you typed. Turn off to stop the prompt.

While typing a long word, selecting it and pausing inserts page groups of words that start the same way but end differently — plurals, verb forms, and longer words — highlighted in blue. An extra Select steps past them if the pause was unintentional. English and Spanish.
How long to hold a selection before the related-words pages appear. Separate from the capitalized-forms delay in Keyboard Setup.
Bundles recent debug logs into a file you can send via email or any sharing app — useful if you\'ve run into a problem.
No debug logs are available to share.
JustType crashed recently. This report contains only the error details and your device model — no text you typed. Thanks for helping us fix it!
Sending a quick crash report helps us fix the problem. It includes only the error details and your device model — never anything you typed.
JustType Main Database Words in Frequency Class %d\n
Press UnDo to close this message
JustType needs permission to display over other apps. This enables advanced input methods like Directional Selection. You can grant this permission now or later in system settings.
This will change how the letters are arranged on your keyboard, and will certainly require time to get used to it. Would you like to try it for a while?
Controls the language used for all on-screen key labels, menus, help text, and messages. Choose System Default to follow your device language, or pick a specific language.
Selects which word database is used for typing words with the JustType keyboard, and which accents LETTER SPELL MODE offers. Changing it reloads the keyboard onto that language.
Only affects Spanish. Picks your regional variety so region-specific word forms (e.g. Spain\'s vosotros forms) sink to the bottom of the selection list. \"General\" keeps all regions equal.

Only affects languages whose accented letters have their own keys (e.g. Spanish). When ON, accented letters appear on their own keys for the most efficient typing. When OFF, the keyboard shows only the base letters — accented words are typed with their base letters and chosen from the selection list.

Available when accented characters are shown on keys. When OFF, a word typed without its accents still appears in the selection list, slightly lower — typing q-u-e also offers qué. Turn ON only if you always type accents exactly; the reward is a very small efficiency gain.

Languages like Vietnamese type each syllable’s tone as its own key press — the tone’s symbol is shown at the bottom of its key. Choose how those symbols are labeled: the bare tone marks, the digits used by the VNI typing method, or the letters used by Telex.

How the Select key steps through the word list. List-based: each press moves down the list one word. Page-based: after stepping past the first listed words, the next press shows the following six words on the letter keys — press a key to choose its word, press Select again for the next six, or Delete to go back.

With Page-based Word Selection, how many words the Select key steps through one at a time before switching to pages of six on the letter keys. Set to 0 to show pages immediately on the first Select press.

Each language has its own Optimized letter arrangement. If you have memorized one language\u2019s arrangement, you can keep using it for every language you type in \u2014 word prediction still uses the language you selected. Match typing language switches the arrangement automatically.

Choose between Optimized (letters grouped by frequency for faster typing) and Alphabetical (letters in A-Z order for a more familiar appearance). The Optimized arrangement is more efficient, requires fewer keystrokes, and is recommended for most people. Changing this is reversible and can be tested before confirming.
Sets how much of the keyboard\'s width the key grid takes; the word list gets the rest. Increase for larger, easier-to-read keys; decrease to give the word list more room.
When ON, pressing Enter inserts two line breaks instead of one, creating a visible blank line between paragraphs. Useful for drafting emails or documents with paragraph spacing.

When ON, each word is spoken aloud as soon as it is finalized — after you Select it and then as soon as you type the first key of the next word (or the Auto-Speak Delay is enabled and times out). This helps verify that the correct word was selected without having to look at the text field each time.

When ON, once a stored phrase is Selected in the Selection List, it is spoken aloud after the Auto-Speak Delay elapses. This lets you speak a stored phrase that you recall without having to type a following key first.
When ON, each completed sentence is spoken aloud after it is finalized by adding a period, exclamation point or question mark. Allows you to automatically speak each sentence as it is completed.
When ON, punctuation characters (period, comma, etc.) are spoken by name when they are output. Useful for verifying that the intended punctuation was typed.
Chooses the small animated icon shown in the top-right corner of the keyboard while speech is being read aloud. The icon lets people nearby see that JustType is speaking.

The number of seconds that JustType will wait after a word or abbreviated phrase is selected before automatically speaking the selected word or phrase. Set to OFF (0) to disable automatic speaking. When the Auto-Speak Delay is disabled, the selected word or phrase will only be spoken when you begin typing the next word.

As you are typing a word, JustType figures out all the possible words in the database that match the keys you have typed so far. JustType can also determine what all the letters are that come next in any of the words that you might be typing. When \"Next-Letter Hints\" is ON, JustType will \"highlight\" each of those letters on the keyboard by displaying these \"Next-Letters\" in bold font, while all other letters are \"grayed out.\" Turning \"Next-Letter Hints\" ON can help guide you as you spell longer words — if you have entered the correct key sequence so far, the next letter of your word will be highlighted. If your next letter is \"grayed out,\" you probably need to back up a little and fix a typing mistake (or add a new word that is not yet included in the database). When ALL of the letters on a key are \"grayed out\" it will not do anything if pressed (and if \"Error Beep\" is ON, you will hear a short beep that can help alert you to this).
When ON, a strip above the keyboard shows the sequence of keys you have pressed for the current word. Helps you track your progress and spot errors.

Sets the height of the key history strip above the keyboard. You set the height as a multiple (from 0.25 to 1.0) of the height of the keys in the keyboard. Increase for a taller, more readable strip; decrease to save screen space.

When ON, the key history strip automatically reduces its height for longer words so that all of the keys pressed fit on the display. When OFF, the strip always uses the full configured height, and earlier keys scroll off to the left for longer words.

When ON, each key in the history strip marks the letter that the currently selected word takes from that key, so you can see how the word is being formed. The marks follow along as you move through the selection list. When OFF, history keys show their letters with no marking.

When ON, rotating to landscape moves the key history to a column beside the keyboard, using the extra horizontal space and leaving the keys larger. When OFF, landscape keeps the horizontal strip above the keyboard, the same as portrait. Portrait is not affected.

When ON, the most recently pressed key in the history strip is outlined in blue, so you can always tell which end of the strip is newest — especially helpful when the history runs vertically in landscape. When OFF, all history keys look the same.
Sets the text size of the word list next to the keys. Increase for easier reading; decrease to fit more words on screen at once. In scanning layouts, larger text also means fewer words per column.

When ON, tapping on an existing word in the text field automatically loads it into the selection list so you can cycle through alternatives, extend the word by typing additional letters, or shorten it by hitting the UnDo key. When OFF, you must manually initiate editing of existing words by pressing the Select key. When \"Auto-Load\" is ON and Edit Mode is used to move the cursor into a word, the word will be automatically loaded when you return to the Main keyboard (by hitting \"BACK TO MAIN\").

When ON, the selection list includes any Capitalized Forms of a word that are available (e.g., \"brown\" for the color, and perhaps also \"Brown\" for \"Ms. Brown\"). When OFF, only the default capitalization of each word is shown in the list, and the SHIFT or CAPS LOCK functions must be used to create Capitalized Forms when desired.

When ON, Capitalized Forms of a word are not added immediately when the word is Selected — they are only added for the Selected word after the \"Delay to Add Capitalized Forms\" elapses. This keeps the selection list shorter (fewer words to step over), while still making other forms available when wanted.

The number of seconds to wait before displaying Capitalized Forms of a word once it is Selected in the selection list. This Delay only applies when \"Wait Until Word is Selected to Add Capitalized Forms\" is ON, and the currently selected word has one or more variant Capitalized Forms. When this Delay is set to OFF (0), available Capitalized Forms are shown immediately (as soon as a word is Selected).

When ON, the abbreviation that is associated with a phrase entry (e.g., \"CMBL\" for \"Call me back later. \") will be shown in the selection list (along with the phrase itself if \"Show Phrase in Selection\" is also ON). When OFF, phrase abbreviations are not shown in the selection list.

When ON, multi-word phrases that have been added with an associated abbreviation (e.g., the phrase \"Call me back later.\" that could be abbreviated as \"CMBL\") are shown in the selection list. When OFF, only the abbreviation is shown.

There are four adaptive input methods that can be used to activate keys, that can be used in addition to any touchscreen method that might be used. These adaptive methods include:
(1) Head Tracking (move a cursor in response to head movement)
(2) Joystick (requires an external joystick)
(3) Single-Switch Scanning (single-switch linear scanning of the 8 keys)
(4) Two-Switch Selection (a sequence of three activations of either of two switches immediately selects one of the 8 keys)
(5) (None - use only one of the touchscreen methods, either Direct Selection or Directional Selection).

The Head Tracking input method requires that the \"HeadBoard\" application (also available from the Continuous Path Foundation) is also installed and configured on your device (just follow the prompts when installing HeadBoard). The HeadBoard app uses the front-facing camera to track your head movement, and move an on-screen mouse cursor in response to it. This cursor appears whenever you are operating any software on your device OTHER THAN THE JUSTTYPE KEYBOARD ITSELF. When the cursor enters the keyboard, its exact location is no longer displayed. This is because keys are pressed just by moving your head in the general direction of the key you want to press. You don\'t have to be very precise — just move your head from the \"resting area\" (the center of the keyboard) in the direction of the key (the \"compass direction\" of the key from the center of the keyboard). As soon as the key turns green, move back toward the center. The key will be activated, and you can move directly toward the next key you want to press. If you accidentally activate the wrong key, just go up to the \"Undo\" key to remove that keystroke.

The Joystick input method requires that you use an external Bluetooth joystick installed and configured on your device. JustType will display an on-screen mouse cursor that will move in response to how you move the joystick. This cursor appears whenever you are operating any software on your device OTHER THAN THE JUSTTYPE KEYBOARD ITSELF. When the cursor enters the keyboard, its exact location is no longer displayed. This is because keys are pressed just by moving the joystick in the general direction of the key you want to press. You don\'t have to be very precise — just move from the \"resting area\" (the center of the keyboard, where the joystick is close to its center position) in the direction of the key (the \"compass direction\" of the key from the center of the keyboard). As soon as the key turns green, move back toward the center. The key will be activated, and you can move directly toward the next key you want to press. If you accidentally activate the wrong key, just go up to the \"Undo\" key to remove that keystroke.

Single-Switch Scanning displays the keyboard as one or two horizontal rows of keys that are scanned (highlighted) in sequence. This allows you to close a single switch to activate the key that is currently highlighted. Because the JustType keyboard only has eight keys, it is easier and more efficient to just scan all the keys in sequence rather than arrange them in multiple rows and use some kind of \"row-column scanning\" that might be used on a keyboard with many more keys. The switch itself can be an external Bluetooth switch that has been installed and configured on your device. If you don\'t use an external switch, you can set up the \"Touchscreen Switch\" so that you can use the bottom of the device screen as your switch and just tap the screen to close the switch.

Two-Switch Selection is different from scanning methods: it uses two different switches (a \"green\" and a \"red\" switch, though the actual color of the switches doesn\'t really matter), and selecting a key requires a sequence of three switch hits on one of the two keys. The keys are each highlighted in either green or red — and all you do is hit the switch that matches the color of the key you want. At the start of a sequence, four of the keys are highlighted in green and the other four in red. Let\'s say the key you want to press is highlighted in green at this point — then you start by hitting the green switch. Then the four keys that were red stop being highlighted, and two of the keys that were green now turn red. Again, just keep hitting the switch that matches the color of the highlight on your key. After the second switch hit, there will only be two keys left — a green one and a red one — you know what to do. At first, you will find the changing highlighting helpful to guide you. But there is also a setting (\"Show color code band at bottom\") that you can turn ON whenever you want. This will display a rectangle below each key with three color bands, either green or red. The left-to-right sequence of color bands shows the sequence of switches that activate that key. Then you don\'t have to watch the key and think about it: if the band shows green then red then green, just hit the switches green-red-green without waiting, and the key will be activated.

NOTE: When Directional Selection (or the Touchscreen Switch) is turned ON below, JustType will \"capture\" all of the touch actions that are performed on all (or part) of the touchscreen. When this is happening, you are not able to touch and interact with other UI controls that may be displayed on the screen. If you or someone else needs to operate your device and thus needs to be able to interact with the screen, the simplest approach is to open the Functions keyboard and activate the \"HIDE KEYBOARD\" function. When the keyboard is hidden, this screen \"capture\" is paused so someone can interact as usual with whatever is shown on the screen. This also means that Directional Selection (or the Touchscreen Switch) will no longer work until the keyboard is displayed again. The simplest way to bring the keyboard back is by simply touching a text field. If there is a need to also enter text while Directional Selection (or the Touchscreen Switch) is OFF, first hide the keyboard with the \"HIDE KEYBOARD\" function, then go to the system settings and turn Directional Selection (or the Touchscreen Switch) OFF in the JustType settings. When you are done, just go back to settings and turn Directional Selection (or the Touchscreen Switch) back ON again.

When ON, you can tap directly on each key to activate it. This is the default touch-screen input method. At least one of Direct Selection or Directional Selection will always remain enabled so a teacher or clinician can interact with the device directly.

When this method is ON, keys can be activated by swiping anywhere on the keyboard and tracing a stroke in one of the 8 possible directions (toward any of the 8 compass points). A stroke of almost any length, anywhere on the keyboard, will activate the key that is in the same direction relative to the center of the keyboard. For many people, this can be much easier and quicker than having to precisely tap a specific key. At least one of Direct Selection or Directional Selection will always remain enabled so a teacher or clinician can interact with the device directly.

When ON, the touchscreen area at the bottom of the screen acts as a virtual switch, providing switch-style input without requiring any external hardware. Can operate in Single- or Two-Switch mode. When enabled, other settings control the size and behavior of the Touchscreen Switch.
When ON, a short single beep sounds each time a key is activated. Provides auditory confirmation that a key press was detected.
When ON, a short double-beep sounds when a key is activated that is not a \"valid\" key (the key has no effect). Provides an auditory indication that the key pressed was likely not the intended key.

When ON, the \"name\" of each key (the list of the letters on the key, or the name of the function on the key) is spoken aloud when the key is activated. Helps identify which key was pressed when visual identification of the key is difficult.
When ON, punctuation names are included when speaking selected key contents (e.g., \"E F G H apostrophe period\" instead of just \"E F G H\"). Only applies when \"Speak each selected key\" is ON.

When ON, each time you press the Select key, the word that becomes selected in the selection list is spoken aloud. Since the vast majority of the time your intended word will be the first word in the list, turning this ON allows you to focus on the keyboard as you spell each word, and since the word is spoken aloud when you finish typing and hit Select, you don\'t have to keep looking up at the text to confirm that you are getting the word that you intended. When only \"Speak Each Output Word\" is ON (on the JustType Settings page), the word will not be spoken until you start typing the next word. This delays the time the word is spoken, but has the advantage of not speaking a word you don\'t actually want to say, but you have to \"step over it\" to Select a word that is lower down in the Selection List.

When ON, settings navigation prompts (such as \"UI Language\", \"Input Methods\", etc.) are spoken aloud when selected in addition to being displayed on screen. Turn OFF if you prefer visual-only prompts.
When ON, each key that is activated briefly flashes with a visual highlight when pressed. Provides immediate visual confirmation of each key that is activated.

The relative size of the center region where head movement has no effect — where you can just \"rest\" without trying to activate a key, and without worrying about activating a key unintentionally. A larger Resting Zone requires more head movement away from the center to get to where the surrounding keys start to respond to your head movement. Increase the size if the keys start to activate even though you are just trying to rest in the middle. The boundary of each Zone is set as a fraction between 0.0 and 1.0, with 0.0 at the center of the keyboard and 1.0 at the very edge.

The relative distance that you have to move away from the center in order to activate a key. When you enter the Active Zone for a key, the key will turn green. After you enter the Active Zone and a key turns green, you just move back toward the center to activate the key. Decreasing the Active Zone makes it so that you can activate keys with less head movement, but may increase the chance that a key will be accidentally activated.

The relative limit that defines the outer boundary for head movement within the keyboard region. You can pause Head-Tracking by turning your head to the right until the you reach the boundary of the Exit Zone, and then keep your head turned until the Exit Delay time elapses. The keyboard border will start flashing when you reach the Exit Zone. Decrease the size of the Exit Zone to reduce how far you need to turn your head to pause or leave the keyboard. When you move upward (instead of to the right) into the Exit Zone, you can move the cursor out of the JustType keyboard. The keyboard border will start to flash, and then the cursor will appear in the region above the keyboard once the Exit Delay time elapses.

Once a key turns green and you start moving back toward the center, this threshold determines how far you must move back before the key activates. A lower value means keys will be activated more quickly, since it will happen before you have to move very far back toward the center. Setting this value to 100% means that you have to go all the way back to the start of the Active Zone in order to activate the key.

The number of seconds that the cursor must remain in the Exit Zone (with the keyboard border flashing) in order to pause or exit. If the keyboard border starts flashing but you don\'t want to exit or pause, just move your head back toward the center to continue using the keyboard. Once the keyboard border has flashed for the Exit/Pause Keyboard Delay Time, JustType will either (a) pause head tracking and display \"Head Tracking Paused\" (moving to the right) or (b) exit the keyboard into the region above (moving upward). Reverse the process, moving all the way to the left to resume typing (\"un-pause\"), or move down to make the cursor \"push against\" the top border of the keyboard to re-enter the keyboard. Increase the Exit/Pause Delay time (or the Exit Zone size) if pausing/exiting happens too easily.

Adjusts the relative sensitivity of diagonal/corner keys (the \"ordinal\" directions — Northeast, Southwest, etc.) compared to \"cardinal\" keys (straight up/down or left/right — North, South, East, West). For some people, corner keys seem harder to trigger than the straight up/down/left/right keys. Values above 1.0 make it easier to reach corner keys — they become relatively bigger targets relative to other keys. Values below 1.0 do the opposite and make the cardinal directions (up, down, left, right) become bigger targets.

This adjusts the relative ease with which up/down head movement moves the cursor vertically compared to how much left/right movement moves the cursor horizontally. Increase if vertical movements feel sluggish compared to horizontal (or simply if it is more difficult to move your head up and down). Values above 1.0 amplify vertical motion, and values below 1.0 amplify horizontal motion.

Controls how much (or how fast) the cursor moves in response to head movement. Values above 1.0 make the cursor move faster/farther (easier to move larger distances). Values below 1.0 result in slower/smaller cursor movements (for more precise targeting).
When ON, JustType displays a diagnostic overlay on the keyboard with zone boundaries, cursor position, and frame rate information. Useful for troubleshooting head tracking behavior.

The relative size of the center region where joystick movement has no effect — where you can just \"rest\" without trying to activate a key, and without worrying about activating a key unintentionally. A larger Resting Zone requires more joystick movement away from the center to get to where the surrounding keys start to respond to the joystick movement. Increase the size if the keys start to activate even though you are just trying to rest in the middle. The boundary of each Zone is set as a fraction between 0.0 and 1.0, with 0.0 at the center of the keyboard and 1.0 at the very edge.

The relative amount of joystick deflection at which a key becomes armed for activation. When you enter the Active Zone for a key, the key will turn green. After you enter the Active Zone and a key turns green, you just release the joystick back toward the center to activate the key. Decreasing the Active Zone makes it so that you can activate keys with less joystick deflection, but may increase the chance that a key will be accidentally activated.

The relative limit that defines the outer boundary for joystick deflection within the keyboard region. You can move the cursor out of the JustType keyboard into the region above (or below) and use your joystick to navigate your device. When you move upward (instead of to the right) until you reach the Exit Zone, the keyboard border will start to flash, and once the Exit Delay time elapses, the cursor will appear in the region above the keyboard. Decrease the size of the Exit Zone to reduce how far you need to move the joystick to leave the keyboard (or pause the joystick). Although this is probably less useful, you can also pause joystick activity in the keyboard by deflecting the joystick to the right (instead of upward) to exit into the Selection List region. IMPORTANT NOTE: You will also need to open HeadBoard and configure a switch to use with the joystick in order to click (or double-click, etc.) at the joystick cursor location.

The number of seconds that the joystick must remain in the Exit Zone (with the keyboard border flashing) in order to exit or pause. If the keyboard border starts flashing but you don\'t want to exit or pause, just move the joystick back toward the center to continue using the keyboard. Once the keyboard border has flashed for the Exit/Pause Keyboard Delay Time, JustType will either (a) exit the keyboard into the region above (when moving upward) or (b) pause the joystick and display \"Joystick Paused\" (moving to the right). Reverse the process, moving all the way to the left to resume typing (\"un-pause\"), or move down to make the cursor \"push against\" the top border of the keyboard to re-enter the keyboard. Increase the Exit/Pause Delay time (or the Exit Zone size) if pausing/exiting happens too easily.

Adjusts the relative sensitivity of diagonal/corner keys (the \"ordinal\" directions — Northeast, Southwest, etc.) compared to \"cardinal\" keys (straight up/down or left/right — North, South, East, West). For some people, corner keys may seem harder (or easier) to trigger than the straight up/down/left/right keys. Values above 1.0 make it easier to reach corner keys — they become relatively bigger targets relative to other keys. Values below 1.0 do the opposite and make the cardinal directions (up, down, left, right) become bigger targets.

If you want to use a Bluetooth switch, make sure that you have paired it with your Android device as a \"Connected Device\" in the system settings. If you want to use a switch that can be set up in HeadBoard (either a Head Movement switch or a Facial Gesture), then you will need to have configured and then enabled the switch below. Then press the \"Activate Scanning Switch\" button to enter switch assignment mode, and either press a physical switch or perform the HeadBoard action to trigger the switch you want to use. JustType will record which switch you triggered and then use it as your scanning switch.

When ON, the touchscreen area at the bottom of the screen acts as a virtual switch, providing switch-style input without requiring any external hardware. The Touchscreen Switch can operate in Single- or Two-Switch mode. When enabled, other settings control the size and behavior of the Touchscreen Switch.
Choose between Large (bigger keys, easier to read) and Small (more compact, leaves more room for other content to be displayed above on the screen).
The number of seconds that the scanning highlight stays on each key before the scan moves on to the next key. Decrease for faster scanning; increase if you need more time to react.

Extra time (in seconds) added to the first scan step after you press the switch or when the scanning process re-starts. This allows you more time to release the switch and have enough time to press the switch to select the first key when the next scan actually starts. Set to OFF (0) for no extra delay.
When ON, a short beep sounds each time the scan highlight moves to the next key. Provides auditory tracking of scanning progress that can help support visual tracking of the progress of the scan.

When ON, the scanner automatically skips over keys that have no valid next-letters highlighted on the key. Speeds up scanning by skipping over useless keys. This also makes the scan less predictable, so you may want to turn ON the next feature \"Show Next Key to be Scanned\".

When \"Skip Keys with No Valid Next-Letters\" is ON, the progress of the scan becomes less predictable. When \"Show Next Key to be Scanned\" is ON, then whenever one or more keys in the current scan cycle will be skipped, the next key that will be highlighted for selection is shown first with a pale yellow highlight, giving you an advance indication that the key will be scanned next (highlighted in bright yellow) to help you prepare to close the switch when it is actually highlighted.

When you close the switch during a scan, it immediately activates the currently highlighted key. When \"Key Activation Auto-Repeat Mode\" is ON, you can continue to hold the switch closed to automatically repeat activations of that key at the Auto-Repeat Delay Time interval (below). When the word you are spelling has two or more letters in a row that are on the same key, this can be much faster than releasing the switch and waiting to scan from the start all the way back to the same key again and then close the switch a second time. If holding the switch closed and waiting to release it at the right time is not difficult, this is highly recommended since it saves significant time for roughly 17% of the letters you type.

The number of seconds between each repeated key activation when the switch is held down in Key Activation Auto-Repeat Mode. In most cases, it will likely work well to set this to the same time interval as the Scan Step Delay Time.

When ON, pressing the switch to activate the Select key automatically starts a scan of the words shown in the current Selection List. Turning this feature ON means that Selecting a word will ALWAYS require two separate switch closures: once to activate the Select key, and then a second time to Select the desired word when it is scanned in the Selection list. For most people, this will be LESS efficient, but this feature may be worth exploring if: (a) Auto-Repeat Mode is not a viable option for you (in that case, simply holding the switch closed on the Select key achieves the same thing but more efficiently); (b) the Scan Step Delay needs to be rather long, so typing additional letters of a word to shorten the Selection List is time-consuming; and (c) you are able to keep an eye on the Selection List as it changes and notice when your word appears (potentially lower in the list).

When scanning continues but no key is Selected, this is the number of times the scanning will cycle through all of the keys before automatically stopping. Set to 0 for \"infinite\" scanning (scanning only stops when you press the switch to activate a key, and then it re-starts). Reduce the number of repeat cycles if you find the repeated cycling distracting. Once scanning stops, just press the switch once to re-start scanning.

This setting enables the system to ignore rapid repeated switch activations within a short time window. Increase this time if your device registers double-taps or multiple presses when you are simply trying to do a single closure of the switch. The default is 120 ms.

If you want to use a Bluetooth switch, make sure that you have paired it with your Android device as a \"Connected Device\" in the system settings. If you want to use one or more of the switches that can be set up in HeadBoard (either a Head Movement switch or a Facial Gesture), then you will need to have configured and then enabled the switch(es) below. Then press the \"Activate (Red or Green) Switch\" button to enter switch assignment mode, and either press a physical switch or perform the HeadBoard action to trigger you want to use. JustType will record which switch you triggered and then use it as your scanning switch.

When ON, the touchscreen area at the bottom of the screen acts as a virtual switch, providing switch-style input without requiring any external hardware. The Touchscreen Switch can operate in Single- or Two-Switch mode. When enabled, other settings control the size and behavior of the Touchscreen Switch.

When ON, holding either the Red or the Green switch causes repeated activations of that switch at the Auto-Repeat Switch Delay Time interval. Useful when switches are easier to hold closed (and release) than it is to press the same switch repeatedly. For example, activating the Select Key is done with three activations in a row of the Green Switch. With Auto-Repeat Switch Activations, this can be done by just holding the Green Switch closed for the time required. Note: When both Auto-Repeat Switch Activation and Auto-Repeat Key Activation are turned ON, then once a three-switch sequence of switch activations is complete, the first key activation is triggered, and continuing to hold the switch closed will generate repeated key activations.
The number of seconds between each repeated switch activation when a switch is held down in Auto-Repeat Switch Activation mode.
When ON, the third switch closure of each three-switch sequence can be held closed to automatically repeat activation of the key just selected. Speeds up typing for experienced users.
The number of seconds between each repeated key activation when Auto-Repeat Key Activation mode is ON and the third switch closure is held closed.
When ON, a short beep sounds each time a switch is closed. Provides auditory confirmation that each switch closure was detected.

When ON, a colored band with a sequence of three green or red segments is displayed below each key, showing the sequence of switch activations that activates that key. This helps to memorize the sequence for each key and speed up input, since you can plan the sequence of switch activations without waiting to see how the key highlight colors actually change.

Each key activation using Two-Switch Selection requires a sequence of three consecutive switch activations. There may be times when you start to enter a switch sequence to activate a key but turn your attention to something else before all three switch activations are entered. When you come back to typing, this may be confusing, or you may simply want to type something different at that time. When the \"Two-Switch Selection Reset Delay\" is set to something other than 0 (which is \"OFF\"), then if you pause in entering a switch sequence for longer than the Reset Delay, the unfinished switch sequence will be canceled and any red and green highlighting will disappear. When you are ready to resume typing, press either switch and the red and green highlighting will be restored to the keys so that you can start a new switch sequence and type the next key.

In case the system fails to detect when a switch is released, this is the number of seconds that the system will wait until deciding to treat what seems to be a continuously closed switch as a \"stuck switch\" and just ignore it. This prevents \"runaway input\" if a switch malfunctions or is accidentally held closed. Set this time higher if it triggers when you are intentionally holding a switch for long periods.

Touchscreen Switch allows you to use the lower portion of the screen as a switch input. When used with Single-Switch Scanning, the entire width of the display is used for a single switch that can be tapped anywhere in the green area shown. When used with Two-Switch Selection, the left half of the display is used for the Green switch, and the right half is used for the Red switch.

To create a single switch, choose Single-Switch (a single, green on-screen touch area is defined at the bottom of the touchscreen, extending across the entire width of the screen). This switch can be used for Single-Switch Scanning or as a Selection Switch for Head-Tracking or Joystick input. To create two separate switches, choose Two-Switch (two adjacent on-screen touch areas are defined at the bottom of the touchscreen, extending across the entire width of the screen, split into left and right halves that function as the Green and Red switches for Two-Switch Selection).

The Touchscreen Switch is always placed at the bottom of the screen to make it easy to activate the switch(es) without unintentionally activating something else on the screen. It also occupies the entire width of the screen. This setting lets you define how tall the touchscreen switch area is. The height is set relative to the height of each row of keys on the JustType keyboard, so setting the height to 1 makes it as tall as the bottom row of the keyboard, and 3 makes it as tall as all three rows. You can set it to anything from 0.5 to 4.0, using decimal values to get exactly the height that works best.
When ON, the touchscreen switch area briefly flashes when tapped, providing visual confirmation that the touch was registered and the switch was activated.
When ON, a short beep sounds when the touchscreen switch area is tapped, providing auditory confirmation that the touch was registered and the switch was activated.

This setting enables the system to ignore rapid repeated switch activations within a short time window. Increase this time if your device registers double-taps or multiple presses when you are simply trying to do a single closure of the switch. The default is 120 ms.

When Overlay Mode is ON, the Touchscreen Switches do not take up any screen space, they are shown as a translucent overlay, beneath which the entire screen is still visible. The JustType Keyboard appears in its usual place at the bottom of the screen. The touchscreen switches still capture all touch events in the area occupied by the switch overlay, so whatever is beneath the touchscreen switch area can be seen but will not respond to touches (which are captured by the Overlay switch area). Even if you do not intentionally turn Overlay Mode ON, it will be automatically turned ON if the height of the combined touchscreen switches and JustType keyboard area (including the Key History display, if shown) extends higher than two-thirds of the total available screen height.

The number of seconds that the Touchscreen Switch overlay remains visible after being displayed when no switch activations are received. The overlay shows the Touchscreen Switch areas on screen. After the timeout, it becomes fully transparent so the switch areas are no longer visible, but the Touchscreen Switch will still remain active.

This setting enables the system to ignore rapid repeated key activations within a short time window. Increase this time if your device registers double-taps or multiple presses on a key when you are simply trying to tap it once. The default is 120 ms.

When ON, holding your finger on a movement or scroll key of the navigation keyboard automatically repeats that key at the Auto-Repeat Delay Time interval (below). This can be much faster than tapping the same key repeatedly, for example when moving the selection across several elements or scrolling through a long list. Keys that perform one-time actions (like Tap or Home) never repeat.
The number of seconds between each repeated key activation while your finger is held on a repeatable key of the navigation keyboard.

This setting enables the system to ignore rapid repeated screen swipes within a short time window. Increase this time if a single swipe gesture is registering as multiple inputs. The default is 120 ms.

The minimum distance that a screen swipe is required to cover in order to register as a swipe. Decrease to make swipes easier to trigger with smaller movements; increase to prevent accidental swipes. This value is set by adjusting the slider setting so that the length of the slider setting on the screen matches to the desired minimum swipe length.

When ON, the words contained in the built-in JustType word dictionary are included in the words that JustType can spell. Turn this OFF only if you want to limit the words that can be generated to only those contained in selected vocabulary lists (and/or Custom Words).
When ON, the words that you have added manually (via the Add New Word function on the Navigation page) are included in the words that JustType can spell.

When ON, the Selection List will also include multi-word abbreviation/phrase pairs that you have added manually to the dictionary (via the Add New Phrase function on the Navigation page) when you type the associated abbreviation.
When ON, the following features are enabled to restrict the words that JustType displays or generates to words that are more common.

When ON, next-letter hints are no longer shown for words below a minimum frequency threshold. Higher values show hints only for more-common words, reducing clutter so that the hints shown will stand out more.

When ON, JustType database words below a minimum frequency threshold are excluded from the Selection List. This can be useful to limit the number of rare or obscure words that show up in the Selection List in order to emphasize more-often-used vocabulary, or to restrict the list to more common words when learning how to spell.

When ON, words that were filtered out by the frequency filter are still shown at the end of the selection list (after all qualifying words). This allows you to still access less common words, but without having them clutter the top of the list.

When ON, this enables JustType to show a second type of \"Accented\" Next-Letter Hints for selected groups of words. (Next-Letter Hints are described in the \"JustType Display\" settings.) \"Accented\" Next-Letter Hints are displayed by showing a letter on a key in a bold, DARK RED font so that they stand out from \"ordinary\" Next-Letter Hints. The following settings enable you define the specific groups of words that will be displayed with Accented Next-Letter Hints so that they naturally draw attention when typing with JustType. When someone is trying to learn new vocabulary, this can help by making the Next-Letter Hints for those words really stand out.

The fewer the number of words shown with Accented Hints, the more the Accented Hints will stand out. The purpose of this setting is to help keep Accented Hints as effective as possible by turning it off for words that someone already \"knows.\" JustType keeps track of how many times a word has been spelled by typing it in with JustType. This setting assumes that the spelling of that word is likely already \"known\" once that word has been typed in a certain number of times. If that is true, Accented Hints would no longer be needed for that word. This setting lets you choose a number \"N\" where once a word has been spelled \"N times\" then Accented Hints are turned off for that word. If N is set to 0, this feature is disabled, meaning that Accented Hints will still be shown for all words in selected vocabularies, no matter how many times they have been spelled.

When set to a value above the maximum frequency class (slider all the way to the right), this feature is OFF. When set to a frequency class, Accented Hints will be shown ONLY for Main Database words that are at least that frequent (or higher).

When set to 0, this feature is OFF (disabled). When set to a higher frequency class (a number from 1 to 14), only lower-frequency words will be displayed with Accented Hints when typed. Combining this with the \"Minimum Frequency for Accented Hints\" allows you to limit Accented Hints first to very common words, and then as those are learned, limit Accented Hints to limited groups of lower frequency words (even just one frequency class at a time). The lower the frequency class, the more words it will contain.

The fewer the number of words shown with Accented Hints, the more the Accented Hints will stand out. The purpose of this setting is to help keep Accented Hints as effective as possible by turning it off for words that someone already \"knows.\" JustType keeps track of how many times a word has been spelled by typing it in with JustType. This setting assumes that the spelling of a word is likely already \"known\" once that word has been typed in a certain number of times. If that is true, Accented Hints would no longer be needed for that word. This setting lets you choose a number \"N\" where once a word has been spelled \"N times\" then Accented Hints are turned off for that word. If N is set to 0, this feature is disabled, meaning that Accented Hints will still be shown for all words in enabled frequency classes, no matter how many times they have been spelled.

One of the features of JustType is designed to support learning literacy skills. One way to help with this is to be able to specify specific lists of words so that JustType can make them easier to enter. This is done by importing files that contain a list of words, and that defines an \"Imported Vocabulary\" that is identified by the name of the file. Then any number of these Imported Vocabulary sets can be Enabled (or disabled), both for whether the word shows up when typed and separately, whether Accented Hints are shown when it is typed. Words from the JustType Database (even words not contained in any Imported Vocabulary) can also be Enabled (or disabled). When \"Promote Words from Active Imported Vocabularies\" is turned ON, words contained in Imported Vocabulary lists (that are enabled) receive a ranking boost, which makes them appear higher in the Selection List relative to ordinary JustType Main Database Words.

The relative size of the center region where mouse movement has no effect — where you can rest without worrying about accidentally activating a key. A larger Resting Zone requires more mouse movement away from the center before the surrounding keys start to respond. Increase if keys activate when you are simply resting. The boundary of each Zone is set as a fraction between 0.0 and 1.0, with 0.0 at the center of the keyboard and 1.0 at the very edge.

The relative amount of mouse movement at which a key becomes armed for activation. When you enter the Active Zone for a key, the key will turn green. Move back toward the center to activate it. Decreasing the Active Zone makes keys activate with less mouse movement, but may increase the chance of accidental activation.

Adjusts the relative sensitivity of diagonal/corner keys compared to the straight up/down/left/right keys. Values above 1.0 make corner keys easier to reach (larger targets). Values below 1.0 do the opposite and make the cardinal directions (up, down, left, right) become bigger targets.

Controls how much mouse movement is needed to move the joystick cursor from the center to the edge of the keyboard. Lower values (fewer dp) make the joystick more sensitive — small mouse movements produce large cursor movements. Higher values (more dp) require larger mouse movements to reach the edges.

How long (in milliseconds) you must hold the mouse pushed UP to release the joystick and restore the cursor. A mouse-button press releases it immediately at any time. Increase if you find yourself accidentally exiting; decrease for a faster escape.

How long after a voluntary release (mouse button press or UP-hold exit) before the joystick will recapture the mouse on hover. Prevents the joystick from immediately grabbing the cursor back when you intended to use it. Set to 0 to recapture instantly.

You can completely backup JustType, including everything you have added or modified: Vocabulary Modules, Custom Words, Abbreviated Phrases, all of your settings, and all of the modifications that are made to the Main JustType Database to reflect how your individual use of JustType. All of the data is written to a folder that you select — either on your device or in a Google Drive folder that you can access. Then later, if you need to, you can use the files saved in the folder to restore JustType, or set JustType up exactly the same way on a different device.

To create a backup (or update an existing one to reflect additional changes):
(1) Press the "CREATE BACKUP NOW" button. If you have already backed up JustType before, this will update that backup to include all the changes that may have happened since the last time JustType was backed up.
(2) If you have not created a backup before, the "CREATE BACKUP NOW" button will take you to a standard Android dialog where you can select the folder to store the backup. Navigate to the folder and press the "Use this folder" button. If/when a prompt appears asking for permission to "Allow JustType to access files in JustType backups?", press "Allow".
(3) You will return to the previous screen, which will show the selected folder. In the future, you will also see the date and time of the last backup created in the folder.
(4) Press the "CREATE BACKUP NOW" button again to create a complete backup in the selected folder. This will automatically be the backup that will be used if you later want to restore JustType.

If something has happened to your device that has, for example, forced you to re-install JustType, you may want to restore your JustType data from a previous back-up. Please be aware, if you haven\'t lost your data and you do this, you will lose any changes in your data since the backup was created. But if you need to restore your data from a previous backup:\n(1) Press the \"RESTORE FROM BACKUP\" button. (It will be greyed out if you haven\'t created a backup yet.)\n(2) A prompt will pop up, asking \"Restore backup? This will overwrite current data. A restart may be needed to reload data.\" As long as you are sure you want to do this, press \"RESTORE\".

When you turn \"Use Advanced Backup & Restore\" ON, you are able to create and load different back-ups of JustType that may be used on different devices. This can be helpful if, for example, you are a teacher or technical support person, especially since these backups can be created on a shared Google Drive. This means you can back up someone\'s device to a shared drive, load that backup into your device and edit it (for example by creating and adding new Vocabulary Modules, Custom Words, Abbreviated Phrases or adjusted Settings), and then save it and reload the edited version from the individual\'s device.\n\nIf you are just using JustType for yourself, it is probably best to just leave the \"Advanced\" mode turned OFF. Then you will always backup to the same location, and if needed, restore from the latest backup.
